Metadata.title: {name} — Space for what’s next
Metadata.description: An architectural Next.js starter with considered typography, coastal colors, and components made to become yours.

Home.title: Space for
Home.description: A little structure. A lot of possibility. Start with a calm, architectural foundation, then make it entirely your own.
Home.featureOneText: Color, space, and typography come from editable tokens. Change the source and the interface follows.
Home.featureTwoText: Useful, accessible building blocks. Enough personality to begin, enough flexibility to grow.
Home.featureThreeText: Modern Next.js, three languages, light and dark themes, offline support, and Playwright checks.
Home.ctaText: Replace the name, choose your colors, and build the thing only you can build.
Home.forkNote: Save your configuration, then create a GitHub fork with that saved version.

System.title: A language for the details.
System.description: A practical collection of tokens, type, and components. Use what helps, change what doesn’t.
System.paletteText: Chalk, cobalt, lavender, and coral. Each color has a job, in light and dark.
System.copyFailed: Copy unavailable. Select the value instead.
System.typeText: Newsreader gives headings a literary warmth. Inter keeps the everyday details clear. Both are hosted locally.
System.componentsText: These are working examples, ready to reuse in your own pages.
System.notification: A small detail, taken care of.
System.dialogText: Native dialog behavior keeps keyboard focus inside, supports Escape, and returns you to the trigger.
System.formTitle: A form, with a clear purpose.
System.formNote: This is a local component demo. No information is sent to a server.
System.formSaved: Example saved in this page. No information was sent.
System.accordionTitle: Can I make this my own?
System.accordionText: Yes. Start with the brand configuration and design tokens. The guide shows where everything lives.
System.spacingText: A small, consistent scale keeps layouts composed, from a phone to a wide screen.

Guide.title: A starting point, not a finish line.
Guide.description: Make the template yours in a few deliberate steps. There are no accounts or external services to configure first.
Guide.oneText: Use Node.js 24. Install the locked dependencies, then start the development server.
Guide.twoText: Change the name and source link in the site configuration. The brand is shared across navigation, metadata, and generated icons.
Guide.threeText: Edit the design tokens, or open Customize UI while running the development server. Preview changes, export JSON, or save them to the project.
Guide.fourText: Run lint, type checks, and the Playwright suite. The production build supports Vercel and any compatible Node.js host.
Guide.note: The starter includes no application-specific authentication or user database. Add those when your project needs them.
